content.thinking:
I'm planning the display setup for the dragonbone soul scythe, deciding to mount it upright on a dark stone plinth with a dragon-claw cradle so it touches the floor properly while standing vertically.

For the skeleton I'll keep it minimal with just one root joint plus a "charm" joint for a hanging soul-tassel or chain. I'm mapping out the vertical coordinates for the plinth and shaft, planning to build the dragonbone texture using stacked vertebra-like segments with ridges, relying on safe, well-established geometry calls like sweeps, lathes, and extrudes since I can't test the code before finalizing it.

For materials I'm settling on a cel-shaded toon palette: ivory and dark bone tones, a purple-black metal, gold accents, and glowing teal-cyan soul fire for high contrast against the darker colors. I'm now planning the scythe blade itself — a large curved crescent extending forward from the top of the shaft, sweeping downward toward its tip to create that classic scythe silhouette.

Writing blade outline coordinates...

Still refining blade geometry...

Working out the normal direction so the outline bulges upward from the tangent, then building the polygon by walking the upper edge forward and the lower edge back, merging the tapered tip point so there's no duplicate vertex.

I'm checking the curvature near the tip against the offset width to confirm no self-intersection occurs, since the taper's radius stays much larger than the blade's half-width there.

For coloring, instead of trying to compute distance-to-edge functions directly, I'm thinking about layering a few extruded shapes: an ivory bone-colored core, and a thinner inner crescent strip offset toward the edge that glows teal on both faces, giving a soul-fire slit effect without needing precise per-point distance math.

Now I'm thinking about adding engraved rune details on the blade faces using small textured planes positioned at the flat x-surfaces, oriented outward on both sides so the glyphs read correctly from either viewing direction, with glow applied to make them stand out.

I'm reconsidering where the runes sit relative to the inlay band — the bone band offset is too thin, so I'll simplify by making the inlay a flat dark violet zone instead of a glow, and let the runes themselves carry the glowing color on top of that darker base.

Now I'm tuning the actual thicknesses: body thinner at 0.03, inlay slightly thicker at 0.036, and a thin pale ice edge strip at 0.026, with runes positioned near x=±0.0195. I'm also thinking about adding bone spur spikes along the spine for extra texture.

I'm placing six spikes along the spine pointing up and back, oriented using cone geometry and a direction helper, all centered on x=0. For a dramatic finishing touch, I'm considering a glowing soul orb—violet or teal—caged by curling claw-like bones at the shaft-blade junction, topped off with a dragon skull head assembly.

Thinking through the skull: facing backward and slightly upward, roughly 0.2 meters long, with the blade extending from the nape and a small soul orb held in the jaws for visual counterbalance. I'm building the cranium as a scaled ellipsoid at the hub point, then shaping the snout as a frustum extending forward from it.

Still designing jaw and horn geometry...

Horns curl outward and back with the blade's thickness clearing them, giving a total scythe height around 2.15m which fits the "soul scythe" scale fine. For the base, I'm thinking the shaft should sit on the plinth, maybe letting a butt spike pierce through to the floor at y=0.

The shaft itself I'll build as a dragon-spine curve from y=0.1 to 1.88 with a subtle S-shape, adding vertebral knuckle rings every 0.11m along its length -- roughly 14 small spool-shaped parts to suggest segmented bone.

For each knuckle I'm lathing a tiny bone-spool outline and adding alternating transverse spike pairs to mimic vertebral processes, giving around 12 vertebrae with 24 spikes plus 12 lathed rings.

Now I'm designing the grip zones along the shaft: two wrapped sections painted with dark stripes using a cel-shaded stripe pattern, capped with small gold torus rings rotated flat to form decorative bands at each wrap's ends.

For the hanging charm, I'm planning a joint partway up the shaft that holds a gold ring connected by a short chain to a glowing teal-cored orb, with violet ribbon tassels dangling beneath via a thin swept outline shape rather than flat card frames.

To avoid ambiguity I'll just explicitly pass bone: root on every part except the charm pieces, using a small options wrapper to keep the calls concise.

I'm adding a jaw joint parented to root for the lower jaw parts, giving three joints total, and planning the octagonal stone base/plinth with a lathe profile for a dragon-claw stand.

Now I'm shaping a glowing violet rune ring disc sitting on top of the plinth, plus four curling bone-ivory claws sweeping up around the base to grip the shaft.

Still placing plinth details...

Actually the plaque placement is getting too fiddly given the plinth's small 4cm wall height — I'll drop it and instead give the plinth a stone-like paint treatment using patches and cel-shaded lighting.

Now I'm sketching the skull: glowing teal eye sockets set into brow ridges with horn-like spikes, and building out the cranium and snout as sculpted geometry positioned relative to the head point, painted in a bone tone.

For the mouth, I'm placing rows of fang-like teeth tapering down from the upper jaw with small dark nostril spheres at the snout tip, then starting the lower jaw as a swept shape from its pivot joint.

Now I'm figuring out how to pose the jaw open—rotating it around the X axis by roughly 18-20 degrees so it can hold the orb positioned just in front at the mouth, while being careful that poses applied after building affect only existing parts, and reasoning through the rotation direction given the skull faces backward along -Z.

Working out the tip position after rotation, I get the lower jaw tip around y≈1.793, z≈-0.244, with the upper jaw tip near z≈-0.28, y≈1.905. I'll place the orb slightly in front of the mouth gap, around [0,1.83,-0.31] with a small radius, floating as if being drawn out from between the jaws.

Now I'm planning to surround that soul-orb with supporting detail: thin glowing violet rings orbiting it, rising flame-like wisps, and three curved bone prongs extending from the upper snout tip that curl downward like a claw cage holding the orb in place. Calculating curve points...

Still placing prong angles...

Now I'm designing the orb itself as a layered glow: a small white-ish inner core sphere surrounded by a slightly larger teal translucent shell, with wispy flame-like tendrils in pale cyan-green and violet rising from it to suggest a captured soul.

Adding neck collar details...

I'm checking the blade root placement against the skull geometry, making sure the blade exits cleanly through the cranium at the correct z-depth so it doesn't intersect the skull mesh improperly.

Rescaling the blade curve parameters so the tip length comes out closer to a realistic scythe size rather than an oversized hero weapon, adjusting the u and v functions so the sweep curves downward with the sharp edge on the inner side.

I'm placing small spikes along the blade's upper edge, angling them backward along the normal direction with a slight tilt, then dropping the dragon-wing-finger idea in favor of adding a bone ivory band between the spine and inlay with a rune glyph.

Adding gold rim strips along the inlay edges, thin and slightly proud of the surface, with the various layer thicknesses (body, inlay, gold, edge) set to create subtle depth differences.

For the bone band I'm using a cel-shaded mottled paint texture for a warm bone tone, and giving the teal edge strip a cyan glow to make it feel soul-lit, tuning the extrude s-range so the strip tapers correctly near the ends.

Writing outline helper function...

Pushing sharp-tagged tuples into the typed point array works fine with contextual typing. The tip sits where width hits zero at the blade's end coordinate, and I'm skipping extra embellishments like tip glows or claw details to keep things simple, letting the shaft's pointed base just sink into the plinth.

Now I'm defining the color palette: bone tones with mottled texture, darker shades for joints, teeth, gold with shadow, dark purple, leather with striped texture, and stone mottling, plus starting on flat glow color strings...

Writing rune SVG paths...

Now I'm positioning the rune planes along the blade's centerline at several points, calculating their world coordinates and orientation so each glowing rune faces outward and stays upright, while working out the inlay width scaling at each position along the blade.

Flat cel shading works well here since faces only point ±x, giving a consistent lit/shadow split per side from the key light direction. Now I'm planning a charm hanging off the shaft—a small gold ring attached around y=1.18, with a chain of stacked tori links leading down to a glowing teardrop soul-vial at the end.

Still planning charm placement...

Now I'm placing vertebra segments along the y-axis, spacing them out while carefully avoiding the grip zones and the charm ring position, working out specific y-coordinates for each one.

I'm also planning transverse spikes alternating along the spine—tilted outward on x and a smaller dorsal spine—while noting I should double check the vertebra radius doesn't collide with the shaft's lathe geometry.

For texture, I'm applying a grain pattern to the shaft to give it a bone-like striped appearance. For the grips, I'm sweeping a rod with flat caps for the handle, adding gold torus bands at the grip boundaries, and shaping a flared gold ferrule collar near the pommel with a custom lathe outline.

Now I'm detailing the skull: adding brow-ridge spikes angled forward and up above the eyes, cheek spikes projecting outward, and jaw-hinge flanges pointing back-out, each defined with position, direction, length, and radius. Then I start sculpting the horns using a smooth sweep curve beginning near the skull base.

Now I'm placing glowing teal eye spheres with dark socket depressions embedded into the cranium ellipsoid surface, checking the normalized position confirms they sit just outside the skull surface for visibility.

Next I'm shaping the upper snout as a tapering sweep flush with the cranium top, adding tiny dark nostril bumps near the tip, then building the lower jaw as a separate tapering bone-colored sweep with its own pivot point, planning to add teeth spikes rising from the jaw line.

Writing spike and plinth geometry...

Now I'm roughly tallying up the total part count across the whole model — plinth, rune ring, studs, claws, ferrule, vertebrae with spikes, grips, skull, orb, and blade — to get a sense of overall complexity.

I'm also considering adding a small gold collar band near the blade root for ornamental detail, working out the right offset and thickness so it fits the blade's outline without clipping past the body's edge.

I'll skip the curled soul-wisp tip idea for now, but I'm thinking about adding a handful of tiny floating teal glow motes drifting near the blade for extra atmosphere.

Writing TypeScript imports...

Defining more joints...

Writing crescent shape function...

Setting up the extrude call for the blade body with reduced bevel to avoid issues on thin strips, and tapering thickness so it's thicker at the root and thinner at the tip.

The taper math gets messy once I try matching inlay, gold, and edge thicknesses to the outline's varying y-range, since each layer has its own min/max. Simplest fix: skip per-vertex tapering and just use fixed constant thicknesses for each layer instead.

Now I'm working out the prong geometry, computing catmull-rom spline control points for each prong position around the ring using angle offsets and radial vectors.

Then I'm adding two torus rings near the orb, giving them different rotations so they intersect at angles, finished in a violet glow material.

For the flames, I'm sketching three glow sweeps rising above the orb, but I notice they'd collide with the snout tip geometrically since both reach similar z-depths. I decide to push the orb further back in z to clear the overlap, then recheck the jaw tip and orb bottom coordinates to confirm the spacing now works.

Checking the gap between the snout cone and flame curves, positioning flame bases slightly offset in x around the orb top with curved paths rising toward y=2.0. Settling on violet and teal as the glow flame colors, and now starting to think about the soul wisps.

Moving on to the plinth now, I'm lathing a rune ring around the base at a fixed height using a thin rectangular profile, giving it a glowing violet material and setting the lathe segments to 16 for a smoother round shape, while checking the stone's taper so the ring sits flush on the flat top region.

Now I'm adding four claws curving up from the plinth around the shaft, using catmull-rom paths with tapered radii and pointed tips, plus a ring of eight small glowing teal gem studs spaced evenly around the plinth's side.

Writing the shaft sweep as a simple two-point polyline bone path, then adding the neck collar lathe detail and bone-colored skull paint, and setting up a torus charm ring around the shaft root before finalizing the rune texture code.

Checking that the lathe vertebra outline closes properly on the x-axis, then verifying type compatibility for spike colors and part rotations. I confirm glow works correctly on sweep, lathe, and extrude parts, with shared materials fine for flat colors, and finalize the jaw pose before returning the build.
